criteria.description: Frames the user's question, scope, and suitable research method without silently turning a topical report into a formal systematic review.

anchors.0: The report misses or materially distorts the question, or claims a formal review method it did not conduct.
anchors.1: The question is mostly answered, but scope, method choice, or review-type distinction is materially unclear.
anchors.2: The report answers the bounded question and accurately describes a method suited to its scope and evidence type.

criteria.improvement_guidance: Align the question, evidence method, and description of review status.

criteria.description: Honors the requested or default depth and any explicit length or source constraints while preserving the same evidence-integrity standards.

anchors.0: The report ignores the requested depth or constraints, or treats lower depth as permission for unsupported claims.
anchors.1: The report roughly matches the requested scale but misses a stated constraint or provides little indication of the resulting coverage limit.
anchors.2: The report matches the selected scope and length, or transparently explains a material evidence limit without padding or overclaiming.

criteria.improvement_guidance: Match the requested scale and state how search or source limits affect coverage.

criteria.description: Grounds substantive claims in identifiable, relevant sources; distinguishes discovered records, inspected full text, and limited abstract or secondary evidence; and avoids invented citations or source details.

anchors.0: Substantive claims lack traceable support, citations or details appear fabricated, or the report misrepresents what source material was inspected.
anchors.1: Most claims have identifiable support, but some important evidence is weakly linked, insufficiently verified, or unclear about access level.
anchors.2: Claims are traceable to relevant cited sources, inspected material is represented accurately, and any citation or access limits are explicit.

criteria.improvement_guidance: Tie claims to verified sources and make source-access status explicit.

criteria.description: Critically compares evidence, evaluates limitations using criteria appropriate to source type, and represents disagreement and counterevidence fairly.

anchors.0: The report is an uncritical source list, overstates certainty or causation, or omits material contrary evidence apparent in its cited sources.
anchors.1: Some comparison and limitations appear, but important disagreements, design differences, or alternative explanations are underdeveloped.
anchors.2: The report synthesizes rather than inventories sources, explains material strengths and limitations, and qualifies conclusions to fit the evidence.

criteria.improvement_guidance: Compare findings and methods, include relevant counterevidence, and qualify interpretations.

criteria.description: Makes search choices, remaining uncertainty, and limits on the conclusion legible to the reader.

anchors.0: Material search or evidence limits are concealed and the conclusion is presented as more complete than the work supports.
anchors.1: Some methods or limitations are stated, but a material uncertainty or scope limit is omitted.
anchors.2: The report briefly but clearly states meaningful search choices, uncertainties, and what the evidence cannot establish.

criteria.improvement_guidance: Report material search scope and limits on what the evidence can establish.
